rich_summary: In the Mahaprasthanika Parva, the final earthly journey of the Pandavas begins after the destruction of the Yadavas and Krishna’s departure. Realizing the dominance of Time and the end of their era, Yudhishthira installs Parikshit as king and renounces the world with his brothers and Draupadi. Clad in bark garments, they set out on a great pilgrimage across the earth toward the Himalayas, followed by a mysterious dog. Along the ascent toward Meru, each companion falls due to a subtle moral flaw—Draupadi’s partiality, Sahadeva’s pride in wisdom, Nakula’s pride in beauty, Arjuna’s boastfulness, and Bhima’s gluttony and vanity. Yudhishthira alone continues without looking back. When Indra invites him to heaven, he refuses to abandon the faithful dog, revealing his unwavering commitment to dharma. The dog proves to be Dharma himself, confirming Yudhishthira’s righteousness as he ascends to heaven in his human body.

highlight_spans.why: The opening invocation and title situate the reader in the epic tradition and mark the beginning of the final journey of the Pandavas.
The epic’s name signals the vast narrative tradition whose concluding moral journey unfolds in this chapter.

top_scenes.scene_text: The Pandavas and Draupadi, dressed in bark garments, silently leaving Hastinapura while citizens weep and a lone dog begins to follow them.
High in a barren Himalayan landscape, Draupadi and the brothers fall one by one as Yudhishthira continues walking ahead in stoic determination with the dog beside him.
Indra’s radiant chariot descending from the sky before Yudhishthira, who refuses to board unless the faithful dog may come with him.
